headline: Historical Cabin and Camping Reservations Required
reservation: While park entry is generally open, staying overnight at Camp Misty Mount or Owens Creek Campground requires advance booking through Recreation.gov. The historic stone and wood cabins are highly popular; verify seasonal opening dates and specific amenity levels with official sources before planning a stay.

days.title: Quartzite Peaks and Panoramas

stops.name: Chimney Rock
stops.detail: Hike the moderate East Side loop to reach this dramatic rocky outcrop overlooking the valley.

stops.name: Wolf Rock
stops.detail: Navigate the deep fissures and large boulders of this ancient quartzite formation adjacent to Chimney Rock.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes from Thurmont; mountain roads may be narrow.
days.note: Footwear with significant traction is necessary for the uneven, rocky terrain of the East Side trails.

days.title: Cascades and Conservation History

stops.name: Cunningham Falls
stops.detail: Cross the park boundary to view Maryland's tallest waterfall cascading down a 78-foot rock face.

stops.name: Blue Ridge Summit Overlook
stops.detail: Take a short, accessible walk for expansive views of the surrounding northern Maryland peaks.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; check for local seasonal road closures.
days.note: Cunningham Falls is located within the adjacent State Park; check for separate vehicle entry fees.

days.title: Forest Solitude and Nature Trails

stops.name: Owens Creek Nature Trail
stops.detail: Enjoy a quieter, low-impact walk through the forest canopy to observe local birdlife.

stops.name: Hog Rock
stops.detail: Follow the interpretive trail to this viewpoint to learn about the mountain's geological history.

days.driving: Minimal travel between west-side trailheads; conditions vary by season.
days.note: The west side of the park typically offers a more secluded experience compared to the central visitor area.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Lots at Chimney Rock and the Visitor Center fill by mid-morning on autumn weekends. Have a secondary trail choice ready if the primary lot is at capacity.

intel.title: Mountain Topography
intel.text: Cellular reception is unreliable in the deep hollows and creek beds. Reliable signals are usually found at the higher rocky overlooks like Hog Rock.

intel.title: Valley Services
intel.text: Refuel in Thurmont or Frederick before heading up the mountain roads. No fuel services are available within the national park boundaries.

intel.title: Seasonal Shifts
intel.text: Spring wildflowers peak in May, while foliage typically colors the ridges in mid-to-late October. Plan mid-week visits to avoid the peak weekend traffic of leaf-peeping season.

intel.title: Road Conditions
intel.text: Park Central Road may close during winter weather events or for seasonal maintenance. Always check the official NPS alert page before driving from Hagerstown or Frederick.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental at Hagerstown Regional (HGR) and stop in Thurmont for trail snacks and water before entering the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are sufficient for most roads; ensure brakes are in good condition for mountain descents.
plan.goldenHour: Blue Ridge Summit Overlook provides a westward vista suitable for sunset viewing, weather permitting.
